proposed.sourceName: SeekersGuidance (Hanafi) — 'Is Rennet in Cheese Halal or Haram to Consume?' (Mawlana Ilyas Patel, checked by Shaykh Faraz Rabbani)
proposed.paraphrase: There is a genuine cross-school difference: the Hanafi school permits rennet from non-porcine animals even if not slaughtered per shariah (rennet has no circulating blood, so it cannot 'die'), while the Shafi'i and Hanbali schools differ — creating uncertainty. When the source is unknown it is better to avoid because of this difference of opinion and the doubt therein; porcine-derived rennet is prohibited outright.

proposed.sourceName: Darul Iftaa New York — 'Hanafi Ruling on Rennet from Non-Pork Animals not Zabiha' (Mufti Muajul I. Chowdhury)
proposed.paraphrase: The fatwa notes the Hanafi school considers non-pork rennet pure regardless of slaughter method, whereas the other legal schools regard rennet from an improperly-slaughtered animal as haram and najis; combined with modern extraction contaminating the product with stomach tissue, unknown-source whey is genuinely contested across the schools.

researcherNote: whey seeded general = grade 3 (Questionable — contested). Whey is a cheese byproduct; when the rennet source is unknown the schools genuinely split (Hanafi permits non-pork rennet even non-zabiha; Shafi'i/Hanbali treat it as maytah/haram) and porcine pepsin is a possibility — so mainstream/general status is contested. Two independent tier-1 sources documenting the split. APPROVED by owner 2026-07-01.
